evidence.quote: Your on-premises database is likely to become stale post-cutover since the post-migration AWS database becomes the main database.
Defined checkpoints that set off a rollback during the cutover if certain predefined criteria are met
Sync Back: Available after Cut Over on online jobs that enabled Post Migration Sync Back. Reverses the change-stream direction (target → source).
Restart Forward Sync: Available while Sync Back is running. Flips the direction back to forward (source → target). Used as the rollback path to point the application back at the source.

edits.old: An all-at-once cutover moves every user with a single routing change, while a phased or canary cutover can expose a smaller slice, monitor load, and make routing rollback easier; phased cutover takes more coordination and time and requires dependencies that can split traffic. This does not remove the MongoDB data gate: for the collections included in a mongosync migration, stop source writes and verify the sync before clients use the destination. (high confidence)

edits.old: For MongoDB online moves that use change-stream catch-up, treat cutover as a gated finalization: confirm low or near-zero lag, stop writes to the migrated source scope and let in-flight transactions finish, submit the commit, verify the successful sync and that destination writes are allowed before routing clients, and keep mongosync active until it reaches COMMITTED. The Azure Mongo migration utility similarly gates Cut Over on zero lag for every collection and completion of background index builds. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)
